correctness_confidence.basis: Reconstructed covariance orientation, energy, exponents, adjoint symmetrization, both regularizations, congruence and order of limits. Own exact and numerical checks pass. This remains AI review conditional on cited theorems.

rigor.basis: The proof is complete at research-note level under explicit Hermitian and positive-span assumptions. It avoids unjustified unregularized determinant convergence and makes no quantitative witness-size claim.

novelty.basis: The free determinant identity and e factor are Mai–Speicher; Gaussian approximation and regularization are classical. The candidate contribution is their in-tuple, energy-accounted finite-witness transfer and covariance optimization.

significance.basis: A dimension-independent comparison for a substantial but restricted class. No general complex-tuple theorem, optimal constant, effective auxiliary-size bound, efficient algorithm or operational consequence is established.

reproducibility.basis: Short inspectable proof, exact artifact hashes, retained source/PDF snapshots, own seeded checker with negative controls and machine-readable results; no author checker was read or credited as an independent check.

summary: The final six-page PDF and source support C/e <= F_infty <= C for Hermitian tuples with a positive definite real-span direction. No material error was found. The real-covariance simplification and same-size normal witnesses are valid; the original dilation remains a valid more general transfer device. Quality 9.0/10; AIRR importance 5.1/10, separately judged. The result is a useful technical bridge, not a new capacity identity or a resolution of unregularized Gaussian log-determinant convergence. Novelty is plausible only in this narrow formulation and was not exhaustively certified. Context is shared, and this reviewer suggested part of the final simplification, so independence is involved_in_manuscript. strengths: The comparison factor is independent of d, s and tuple coefficients within the stated class, while all energy costs are explicitly charged.
The upper bound handles arbitrary complex tuples and complex positive semidefinite covariance matrices, including singular covariance.
The regularization remains inside the original coefficient tuple; the proof takes the large-matrix limit before removing the shift.
Real covariance suffices by adjoint capacity invariance and concavity, so the main construction uses normal witnesses without doubling auxiliary size.
The manuscript clearly attributes Mai–Speicher, states the restrictions, and avoids asserting effective size, optimality or a general complex-tuple extension.
weaknesses: Most of the deep analytic content and the numerical constant e are imported from Mai–Speicher; the new bridge is a short consequence after the right regularization is recognized.
The real-span positive-definite hypothesis excludes many naturally traceless or arbitrary noncommutative pencils.
There is no quantitative bound on auxiliary size or conditioning dependence, no covariance optimization algorithm and no proved operational payoff.
The examples verify normalization and scope but do not demonstrate a sharp nontrivial C/F_infty gap or establish optimality of e.
The literature audit is directed rather than exhaustive; related regularization and shifted-determinant literature deserves concise positioning in a future revision.
strong_novelty_candidates: Subject to an independent priority search: the explicit finite-witness transfer inside a Hermitian coefficient tuple with a positive direction, preserving normalized energy and yielding the universal C/e lower bound.

The real-covariance / normal-witness formulation is a useful elementary refinement, derived from prior capacity duality and concavity; it should not be presented as a separate deep invariant or an independent review contribution.
